taxonomic_note: Current Kew recognizes subsp. hallii and subsp. filipes; B009 remains species-level pending a need for subspecies-level field instruction.
look_here_first: HALL'S PANICGRASS: Native small mostly BASAL, stiff blue-green perennial BUNCH (often around 30–60 cm); old basal leaves curl like wood shavings. Flower stalk bears an open but modest ~6–20 cm panicle with stiffer ascending branches and small clustered ovoid spikelets. Confirm a mature spikelet, the shiny fertile lemma and ciliate/hair-fringe ligule with a lens. The existing 3 original photographs teach tuft, leaf curling and actual spikelet; not microscopic anatomy.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Panicum hallii, lists Texas as native, and recognizes subsp. hallii and subsp. filipes. Hagenbuch & Lemke explicitly record multiple Hays County specimens. The same appendix records Blanco County (Lackey 777, SWT). The same appendix records Val Verde County (Labus 301, 326, 352, SWT). Kerr — Singhurst et al. (2010), Kerr Wildlife Management Area natural flora, p. 511, published specimens JS 10677; FG 8249; LS 4050, 4416, 4532. Together Hays, Blanco, Kerr satisfy the 3-county project threshold; historical out-of-zone counties not counted.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

Witchgrass P. capillare is a hairy ANNUAL and much more cloudlike; Kleingrass P. coloratum is a robust African-introduced forage perennial; switchgrass P. virgatum is usually much taller, rhizomatous and has a conspicuous white triangular blade-base hair patch.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Panicum virgatum: Switchgrass is much taller and rhizomatous with a much larger diffuse panicle. Panicum capillare: Witchgrass is annual and strongly hairy with a huge lax panicle; Hall's is perennial, glaucous and stiffer.

measured_species_key_20261023.look_here_first: Look for a small mostly basal stiff, often blue-green perennial tuft; older basal blades curl like wood shavings. Trace a 6–20 cm open but stiff-branched panicle and inspect clustered, appressed oval spikelets. Confirm the short fringed ligule and shiny hard mature fertile lemma rather than guessing from a seedhead silhouette.
measured_species_key_20261023.growth_form: Perennial bunchgrass with persistent basal sheaths and mostly basal leaves; culms 20–80 cm in Kew, often 30–60 cm in Texas field descriptions. No long creeping stolon or extensive rhizome is established by the existing photographs.
measured_species_key_20261023.ligule_collar: Kew GrassBase: ligule a 1–1.5 mm fringe of hairs. Williamson County's subsp. filipes treatment: a 1.2–1.5 mm membranous ligule ciliate from midpoint or below, whitish collar to 1.5 mm. At the attached blade/sheath junction photograph the membrane and hairs separately; do not use subsp. filipes details to assign a subspecies to the species-level card.
measured_species_key_20261023.flowering_architecture: Open pyramidal 6–20 cm panicle with ascending, relatively stiff branches; short-pedicelled solitary/appressed spikelets may overlap in small clusters. Unlike loose tumble-like witchgrass, the flowering head is relatively compact and orderly.
measured_species_key_20261023.spikelet_glume_lemma_awn: Kew species-level: dorsally compressed ovate spikelets 2.2–3.7(–3.9) mm, one lower sterile and one upper fertile floret; lower glume one-third to two-thirds spikelet length, upper glume approximately full spikelet length, each described as 5-veined; lower sterile lemma approximately spikelet length; hardened shiny dark-brown fertile lemma 2–3.5 mm, awnless. The Williamson County subsp. filipes specimen differs (2.1–3 mm spikelets, upper glume 7–11 veins, fertile lemma 1.5–1.8 mm); keep these taxon-concept-specific observations separate.
measured_species_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: P. capillare (witchgrass): hairy annual with broad cloudlike, often detached/tumbling panicle, rather than stiff basal perennial tuft. P. coloratum (kleingrass): robust introduced forage perennial with larger coarse growth and its own glume proportions. P. virgatum (switchgrass): taller often rhizomatous and with blade-base hairs; compare intact basal crown, ligule and mature spikelets.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Hall's panicgrass — photograph-guided field recognition
steps: START with the physically archived whole-habit photograph: trace the relatively small mostly basal perennial tuft and stiff ascending panicle branches; do not infer a rhizome from the photo.
LOOK at the physically archived curled-leaf photograph. Old basal blades can curl tightly, a supporting vegetative cue rather than proof of species identity.

FOLLOW a panicle branch to the actual small oval spikelets in the archived reproductive close-up. Arrows already point to visibly resolved spikelets, but individual glumes cannot be counted at this resolution.
FIELD MACRO HOLD: expose the blade/sheath collar on one plant and measure its approximately 1–1.5 mm fringe of hairs or ciliate membrane at 10–20×; do not put this label on an overview photo.

FIELD MACRO HOLD: photograph intact mature 2.2–3.9 mm spikelets against a millimeter scale, then separated glumes, sterile floret and glossy hardened awnless fertile lemma. Keep species-level characters separate from subsp. filipes measurements.

CHECK the look-alikes: witchgrass (P. capillare) tends to be a hairy annual with a diffuse cloudlike panicle; introduced kleingrass (P. coloratum) is usually much coarser; switchgrass (P. virgatum) is typically taller and often rhizomatous.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Small blue-green perennial basal tuft + relatively orderly ascending-branched panicle + measured true hairy/ciliate ligule and hard shiny mature fertile lemma. No single habit photograph proves the species.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Three physically archived source-licensed photographs and four gross-feature arrows were previously checked. Existing images do NOT resolve the true collar ligule, glume veins, or measured fertile lemma; never annotate those invisible structures. No new physical JPEG or arrow added in this update.
